sentences.text: The front of the skull expands into a circular, spatula-like shape holding twenty-two narrow teeth that point sideways.
The preserved snout contained forty additional tooth sockets, leading to an estimated total of seventy-six teeth in the upper jaws.
Its skull length was estimated to be at least forty centimeters, despite being similar in overall size to large gnathosaurines like Gnathosaurus.
The holotype fossil is an incomplete anterior upper jaw with teeth discovered in a chalkstone quarry near Langton Matravers.
The genus was named in 1995 by Stafford Howse and Andrew Milner.
The specimen was held by the Corfe Castle Museum and the Dorset County Museum in the 1950s before being purchased by the Natural History Museum in 1958.
David Unwin placed it in the subgroup Gnathosaurinae in 2005.
It lived from the Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous periods (Tithonian to Berriasian stages) in what is now the Purbeck Group of Dorset, England.
Its time range is estimated from 143.1 to 137.05 million years ago.
A 2025 phylogenetic analysis suggests Plataleorhynchus falls outside the grouping of all other gnathosaurines.
